request.packet: Approved fictional procedure: Defence responds to the visible public submission; no earlier Defence acceptance is supplied.

evidence.name: fictional-account.txt
evidence.text: Fictional witness Mira states: I saw Fictional Rowan hand the sealed envelope to Fictional Ellis. I do not know what the envelope contained.

request.groundingContext: E-101: permitted for accurately attributing Mira's account and previewing that account; not proof of envelope contents or guilt. The account is disputed. No assertion of complete disclosure is authorized.

payload.text: On this record, the Crown burden is not met; not guilty is the appropriate outcome.

result.content: The Crown and Defence agree that the burden is not met on this record.

findings.text: The Crown and Defence agree that the burden is not met on this record.
findings.explanation: The claim attributes agreement to the 'Defence' party, but no Defence party is included in the approved party roles (only Crown and Ellis as accused are mapped). The only visible public submission is from actor Ellis (the accused), not from a Defence advocate, so it does not establish a Defence party position. While the Crown may adopt its own present stance under the author-adoption exception, asserting that 'the Crown and Defence agree' specifically attributes a position to the Defence that is not supplied to this run. Private submissions and other jurors' ballots remain unavailable.
